summary.text: Bob Latta is the U.S. Representative for Ohio's 5th District, first elected in 2007, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results. An attorney by training, he previously served as Wood County Commissioner and in both chambers of the Ohio legislature. In Congress he serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Energy.

paragraphs.text: Latta was born in Bluffton, Ohio, in 1956; according to his congressional website, he is a lifelong resident of northwest Ohio. He earned a bachelor's degree from Bowling Green State University (1978) and a J.D. from the University of Toledo College of Law (1981).

He worked in private practice as an attorney before entering public office, serving as Wood County Commissioner (1991-1996), in the Ohio State Senate (1997-2000), and in the Ohio House of Representatives (2001-2007).
Latta was first elected to the U.S. House in 2007 and has represented Ohio's 5th District since.

He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Energy and sits on the Communications and Technology and Environment subcommittees; his congressional website also lists him as a Deputy Whip and co-chair of the Rural Broadband Caucus and the Congressional Propane Caucus.

His congressional website says he authored the INFO Act, included in legislation addressing the opioid crisis, and has advanced the Advanced Nuclear Technology Development Act and the Critical Electric Infrastructure Act, both of which it describes as law.
According to that website, Latta lives in Bowling Green with his wife, Marcia; they have two daughters.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 54.3% of the vote to Brian Shaver's 42.6% and Michael Veloff's 3.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
